_doc: SOURCE-CUSTODY-PII-01 · ACT 4 §C + CORPUS-AUTHORITY-01 — corpus admission declaration. Enforced by lib/corpus/admission.ts. A file enters MAIA's knowledge corpus ONLY when a rule names it, its classification permits corpus membership, AND the rule carries a compatible structured authority basis. Absence of any one means EXCLUSION.
_law: Membership and authority must be DECLARED and CHECKED, never INHERITED from location, naming, publication status, or a free-text assurance.
_state: The existing corpus is declared unclassified_legacy, which does NOT admit. This is deliberate: 736 files under data/ain/source have never been classified, and admitting them in bulk to keep the build green would reproduce the defect this declaration exists to close. Classification is per-collection founder work; each reclassification is a governed edit to this file.

_classifications.published_knowledge: ADMITS — authored knowledge intended for MAIA to draw on.
_classifications.third_party_published: ADMITS — third-party published text held under an explicit basis.
_classifications.organizational_public: ADMITS — Soullab's own governed public material.
_classifications.unclassified_legacy: EXCLUDES — present in the tree, never classified.
_classifications.operational_human_record: NEVER ADMITS — known to carry human records.

rules.reason: ACT 4 §C: the historical corpus root. Every file here was ingested by directory convention alone, with no classification and no PII exclusion — the defect this declaration closes. Held closed until each collection is classified on its own evidence.

_authority.soullab_owned: May support published_knowledge or organizational_public when ownership evidence is named.
_authority.public_domain: May support third_party_published only when the work itself—not an image, quotation, or phrase—is evidenced public domain.
_authority.license: May support third_party_published only when the license evidence governs the work and permits the intended corpus use.
_authority.permission: May support third_party_published only when explicit permission evidence for corpus use is named.
